S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in the health or behavior of a family member
patient_info.stressor: When Lissette's husband developed a prolonged need for help with appointments, transportation, and household follow-through, the careful paper-and-calendar systems she had used for years were suddenly no longer enough. Over the next 15 months, the added caregiver and volunteer demands exposed a longstanding vulnerability: she struggled to organize senior-center programs and home tasks, put off paperwork that required sustained concentration, misplaced keys, recipes, church materials, and appointment cards, and became increasingly pulled off track by noises, conversations, or unrelated thoughts. Her daily forgetfulness began to affect bills, errands, family commitments, and volunteer reliability, while her fidgeting and repeated need to get up during meetings drew notice in settings where she had once been steady and composed. After she stepped back from a major intergenerational event because the logistics had become unmanageable, her primary care physician referred her for psychiatric evaluation.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: I came in because I can’t seem to get anything in order anymore—my kitchen table is covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, senior-center notes, and half-finished lists, and I sit there not knowing which thing to do first until the whole day is gone.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: When there’s a form to fill out, insurance papers to read, or a program schedule to put together, I keep finding little reasons to put it off because my head feels worn out before I even start.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m forever hunting for things I just had in my hand, like the car keys, my reading glasses, appointment cards, recipes for the church supper, or the folder I need to take to the doctor’s office.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: If the television is on in the next room or two people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just follows that instead, and then I lose my place in what I was writing or planning.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I’ve missed returning calls, left bills sitting under a stack of mail, forgotten errands I promised my daughter I’d do, and more than once realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: Even when I’m trying to sit politely in a meeting, I catch myself rubbing my hands, tapping my foot, clicking my pen, or shifting around so much that people look over at me.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: During volunteer meetings or even at supper, I keep getting up to check the calendar, look for a paper, refill water, or just move around, even when I know I’m supposed to stay seated and listen.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Even as a little girl, my teachers wrote that I was bright but careless, forgot books and homework, and needed reminders to finish seatwork before I could go outside.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I had to give up leading a big senior-center event, and my daughter has started double-checking bills and appointments because she no longer trusts that I can keep everything straight on my own.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: It has been causing this much trouble for about a year and three months, since my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements.
